title: QBR / Health Check - Avalon Systems
summary: Quarterly business review covering usage trends, cost anomalies, reliability incidents, roadmap alignment, and next steps for a pilot to move inference to Dedicated. Action items captured for cost breakdown, latency benchmark, and security docs.

Dedicated vs Hosted for upcoming pilot
Roadmap alignment and upcoming model updates

transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-06-18
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya, James, Ravi (Redwood) ; Elena, Marco, Sophie, Daniel (Avalon)
Notes/Links: QBR deck link: https://redwood.ai/qbr/avalon-deck (shared), cost CSV: sent post-call

Summary: quick check-in and QBR. high level usage is up ~42% qtr-over-qtr, cost bumped in May due to unoptimized long-context jobs and a couple of high-concurrency bursts. customer interested in Dedicated pilot and wants reassurance on latency and SOC2 evidence.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we'll kick off the QBR, we put a short agenda in the invite. can i get quick intros?
[00:18] Elena: hi, this is Elena Chen, head of MLOps at Avalon. quick note, Marco will jump in on infra questions.
[00:25] Marco: hi all.
[00:27] Sophie: Sophie on DevOps.
[00:28] Daniel: Daniel, PM.
[00:30] Maya: great, from Redwood side it's me, Maya (AE), James O'Neill, our solutions engineer, and Ravi CSM. good to see you.

[02:05] Maya: alright first section, usage and cost trends. over the last quarter we've seen overall token usage uptick - a 42 percent rise, most of that driven by a new feature you shipped in March. does that align with your expectations?
[02:25] Elena: yeah that tracks. we've got a couple new flows that run 16k token contexts for retrieval plus generation. we also had more retries when latencies spiked.
[02:40] James: right, the long context + retries combo is expensive. also i see some heavy synchronous calls at 8-10 concurrent per instance around peak times, which prevents efficient batching and drives per-token cost up.
[03:05] Marco: sorry can you spell that, batching - are you referring to redwood's automatic batching?
[03:10] James: yeah, it's the runtime batching. when requests come in at high concurrency with long context, the effective batch size drops and latency SLOs force less batching. that plus prefix caching misses from varied user prompts equals extra cost.

[05:00] Elena: in May we saw two cost anomalies, a 30% one-week spike. we traced some of that to a background ingestion job that started hitting the API for embeddings with full doc contexts instead of sharded chunks.
[05:18] Maya: okay that makes sense. we can help with recommendations - quantization profiles, suggestion to shard the docs, and also a caching layer for frequently requested prefixes.
[05:35] Sophie: curious on Dedicated - would that lower unit cost for those heavy-embedding workloads?
[05:40] James: yes, Dedicated usually gives better unit economics for steady high throughput because you get reserved GPU pools and can optimize execution kernels. but up-front commit is needed; we can model costs with your actual traffic.

[08:00] Maya: next, reliability incidents. i have notes on two short incidents in May, both 5 to 10 minutes - one region failover and one degraded kernel path during a model rollout. can you describe the impact?
[08:20] Elena: the region failover caused a small % of requests to timeout and we saw an uptick in retries; some user-facing latency blips. the second incident was during your model autoscaling test where p99 jumped and then recovered. overall customers noticed but no data loss.
[08:45] Ravi: thanks for that context. on our side we have post-mortems for both; we'll share the summaries and the mitigations: improved canary gating and fallback to older model variants during kernel regressions.
[09:15] Marco: can you also share the trace logs? we need them for our incident audit.
[09:22] Maya: yes we'll include trace hooks and example traces in the security pack.

[11:00] Daniel: quick question - we have strict requirements for KMS and key rotation. are you able to integrate with our cloud KMS and use customer-managed keys for payload encryption at rest?
[11:12] James: absolutely - Redwood supports KMS/HSM integrations and CMKs for private deployments and Dedicated. we'll include the integration notes. for hosted we have envelope encryption and audit logs; for Private we can do full customer key control.
[11:30] Elena: great, send the compliance docs.

[13:00] Maya: roadmap alignment - we have an upcoming release that improves batching heuristics and a quantization profile tuned for long-context transformer variants in July. that should directly help your long-context costs.
[13:20] James: the optimization targets better KV cache reuse and slightly different kernel scheduling to reduce p95 latency when contexts exceed 8k tokens.
[13:35] Sophie: will that require any client changes?
[13:38] James: minimal - mostly server-side, but we'll recommend minor timeout tweaks and an optional header to signal expected context length so the runtime can pre-allocate.

[15:00] Maya: price discussion - i've pulled some rough models. for your current volume, hosted is still flexible but the Dedicated pilot we discussed would reduce per-token cost by ~18-26% depending on commit size and the success of batching improvements. we can run a modeled spreadsheet and share.
[15:25] Elena: we liked the idea of a pilot where we reserve a small pool and run a two-week benchmark. can we include throughput SLOs and a rollback clause?
[15:33] Maya: yes, typical pilot includes throughput SLOs, agreed rollback, and a go/no-go at the end. we'll put that in the pilot scope.

[17:00] Marco: on the benchmarking - what does the SE team need from us? traffic samples, peak windows?
[17:08] James: traffic profile (RPS over time), example requests (both long-context and short), and preferred test windows. if you can provide a replay of a representative day that helps us simulate concurrency and caching behavior.
[17:25] Sophie: we can get that by monday.

[19:30] Elena: security - SOC2 report, SAML SSO, RBAC, and audit logs are top items. also we need a diagram for data flows for our auditors.
[19:45] Ravi: we'll attach SOC2 summary, SSO guides, RBAC docs, and an architecture diagram that shows encryption at rest and in transit plus KMS flows.
[20:05] Daniel: also any notes on data residency? certain EU customers need EU-only data handling.
[20:12] Maya: yes we have region routing policies and can keep data in specific regions; for Private deployments you can host fully in your VPC. we'll write the residency options in the pack.

[22:00] Elena: one more ask - during the last incident our logs had a couple of garbled names, it made triage slower. is there a way to increase trace verbosity or better labeling?
[22:12] James: yes we can enable richer trace headers for your account and include request ids that tie through the full stack, that'll make cross-service correlation easier.
[22:25] Maya: we'll enable that for your account in staging and share instructions.

[25:00] Maya: any open concerns on roadmap or functionality?
[25:10] Marco: just curious about function/tool calling support - we plan to implement structured tool calls in Q3. how mature is the runtime support?
[25:22] James: we support function/tool calling and structured outputs; runtime handles streaming and partial outputs. we'll demo a short sample in the pilot if you want.
[25:40] Sophie: yes please demo that.

[28:00] Maya: recap and next steps - we'll send the deck, cost CSV, security pack, and pilot scope. James will run the benchmark when you share traffic. Ravi will follow up on scheduling and post-mortem docs.
[28:20] Elena: perfect. also, who should we loop in for procurement if pilot looks good?
[28:28] Maya: i'll include pricing and procurement contacts in the email.

[30:00] Action item readout: Maya runs through action items quickly.
[30:20] Maya: okay thanks everyone. any final questions?
[30:25] Marco: no, thank you.
[30:27] Daniel: thanks all.
[30:30] Maya: cool. we'll follow up by monday with materials.

[45:00] End call.

Transcription notes: there are a few small mis-hearings (e.g., kv cache transcribed as "K V cache" in one internal note). speaker turns occasionally overlap and filler words (uh, mm) appear. references to shared artifacts: QBR deck (link above), cost csv (to be sent), security pack (to be attached).
